messages:
Ethan: quick twilight watch recap — leaving notes for the incoming crew. TL;DR: brief p95 latency spike during EU morning window, a small batch of 503s tied to a KV cache leader election, we mitigated with targeted routing + temporary cache bypass. No active customer-impacting errors now but a few follow-ups needed.

Ethan: timeline: 20:07 UTC incident-bot fired p95 spike alert; 20:09 deploy-bot reported a rollout to model-repo:quant-2 that coincided with increased cache churn; 20:12 we saw the leader election on kv-cluster-eu-1 and 20:13 started routing traffic to secondary pools.

incident-bot: ALERT (20:07 UTC) — latency.p95.inference.euw increased from 180ms -> 720ms over 5m, error.rate 503s 0.9% (service: inference-router). Pager severity: P2.

Ethan: actions taken (in order):
- 20:10: pinned router policy to avoid canary pool (policy id: rt-evade-2301).
- 20:12: applied temporary KV bypass on the affected region: set header X-Redwood-KV-Mode: stale-reads for route /v1/generate for 6m.
- 20:15: scaled up kv-cluster-eu-1 leader candidates + increased election timeout (see command snippet).

Ethan: relevant commands we ran (copy if you need to inspect):
```bash
# check kv cluster leader status
kubectl exec -n infra kv-ops-ctl -- ./kvctl status --cluster eu-1
# scale leader candidates
kubectl scale statefulset/kv-candidates -n infra --replicas=5
# routing change (temporary)
redwoodctl routes set --route inference --policy rt-evade-2301 --region eu-west-1
```

Janelle: can you paste the exact runbook link you used? I'll add notes.

Ethan: runbook I used: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction — I left a quick note at the top: "Used stale-reads header and pinned routing to secondary pools at 20:15 UTC". Also filed a follow-up ticket.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook accessed: kv-cache-eviction by Ethan (20:16 UTC) — automated annotation added to runbook: "Twilight 20:07 evict spike — routing pin applied."

Marco: customers: CS flagged two small customers (acct: polaris-inc, acct: datum-labs) who saw degraded responses. Both are low-volume and we reached out with an FYI — no escalations. Marco will follow-up in the morning for postmortem notes.

Priya: current state check? what still needs ownership from incoming team?

Ethan: current state:
- All routes back to normal p95 ~ 200ms (eu-west) as of 20:42 UTC.
- 503s flattened to 0.02% for the last 30m.
- KV cluster shows stable leader on node kv-0.
- Temporary headers removed at 20:40 and routing policy rolled back at 20:41; I kept a safelist for 30m just in case.

Ethan: outstanding items (short list):
1) Follow-up ticket with perf traces + heap profiles attached -> TICKET-1256 (assigned to Janelle)
2) Validate election params change isn't causing longer-term churn -> Priya to verify during next morning soak window
3) Add a canary-window guard to deployments to avoid deploying model quantization updates during EU morning window -> Ops-sig suggestion, assign to platform backlog
4) Customer follow-ups: Marco to email the two impacted customers with summary and next steps.

Janelle: I'll own TICKET-1256. Plan: collect traces for 20:00-20:30 UTC, grab KV leader metrics (election_count, avg_latency) and correlate with model-repo:quant-2 rollout. ETA 24h.

Priya: I can validate election params tomorrow during the EU soak (08:00-10:00 EU). I'll also add a small probe to detect quick leader flaps and alert earlier.

Ethan: primary/secondary for the next window: Priya as primary, Janelle as secondary. I'm handing off escalation contacts to Priya.

Priya: ack — I'll take primary. Oncall numbers are up to date in the runbook. Quick ask: can someone verify the deploy that ran at 19:58 UTC (model-repo:quant-2) — I want the exact image sha to correlate.

Ethan: image sha: sha256:8a4f2b9c1d (from deploy-bot message at 19:58 UTC). Deploy-bot logs attached in the run.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: model-repo/quant-2 @ sha256:8a4f2b9c1d started (19:58 UTC), finished (20:01 UTC), rollout strategy: slow-canary 10%/min.

Janelle: note for handoff: run the following check if you see p95 rise again —
1) kubectl logs -n inference router-xxx | grep "kv miss"
2) curl -s -H 'X-Redwood-Debug: on' https://router.euw.internal/health | jq '.'
3) Check kv election_count metric: metrics.redwood/kv_election_count{cluster="eu-1"}

Ethan: escalation contacts: Platform on-call (pager: +1-555-0103), SRE lead (Janelle), Prod owner (Marco). All in runbook.

Priya: sounds good. I'll also add a quick throttle on canary rollouts between 06:00-10:00 EU in the deployment guard config. Filing small PR for that now.

Marco: I'll send customer note template tonight and ping CS leads. Will include mitigation steps and offer postmortem call if requested.

Ethan: final handoff note: no active pages, metrics stable, readers ok. Priya taking primary. Janelle secondary. If you see p95 > 400ms or >0.5% 503s for 10m, page P1.

Priya: acked. thanks for the detailed notes Ethan — good context. I'll pick up verification in the morning and close TICKET-1256 after Janelle's analysis.

Janelle: ack — will post findings in TICKET-1256 and link to runbook.

Ethan: leaving: signing off — enjoy the rest of the night. :coffee:
